abstract: Tetraploid potato is highly heterozygous, and its four haplotypes differ in gene content and regulation of gene and isoform expression, yet responses of individual haplotypes to environmental stresses remain poorly characterized. Here, we used long-read RNA sequencing to profile the haplotype-resolved leaf transcriptome of potato cv. Desiree under prolonged heat. Long-read RNA-seq gene counts correlated with short-read RNA-seq at the gene level but assigned far more reads uniquely to individual haplotypes. Under control conditions, allelic imbalance was widespread, whereas after prolonged heat, most alleles responded in the same way across haplotypes. Allele-specific exceptions point to candidate alleles for heat tolerance. We identified a heat-inducible, redox homeostasis-related N2-acetylornithine deacetylase allele and confirmed its allele-specific promoter activity in planta. Heat stress induced alternative isoform usage of 390 genes. Among these, we identified a heat stress upregulated heat shock protein 40 chaperone gene isoform that, unlike its alternative splicing isoform, localizes to the nucleus instead of to the cytoplasm. These results show that in a polyploid crop haplotype-resolved long-read transcriptomics can help in identification of alleles for stress tolerance breeding.
